title: Toilets don’t flush the opposite way south of the equator
body: The Coriolis effect, caused by Earth’s rotation, is real and steers huge weather systems: hurricanes spin anticlockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and clockwise in the Southern. But it only matters over large distances and long times. In a sink or toilet that drains in seconds, it is far weaker than the shape of the bowl and the way the water entered. Only carefully controlled experiments with very still water can detect it.

slides.question: Why doesn’t the Coriolis effect decide which way your sink drains?
options: It only acts on salt water
It cancels out at most latitudes
It is far too weak at that small scale
Sinks drain too fast for any force
slides.explanation: The Coriolis effect only matters over large distances and long times. In a bowl that empties in seconds, its shape and the way the water entered matter far more.

slides.heading: Which one is not steered by the Coriolis effect?
slides.explanation: Hurricanes, ocean currents and shells flying for kilometres move far enough for Earth’s spin to bend their paths. A bathtub empties in seconds, where the effect is negligible.
